text: Why is rho(W_rec) < 1 described as 'sufficient but not necessary' for the ESP of a tanh reservoir?
choices: Because the leak rate can cancel any spectral radius, making the condition meaningless
Because for large-amplitude inputs the tanh derivative grows above 1, expanding the state
Because rho < 1 is in fact neither necessary nor sufficient; only the trace matters
Because tanh saturation drives derivatives toward 0, shrinking the effective Lipschitz constant, so the ESP can still hold when rho > 1 under strong inputs
explanation: When strong inputs push neurons into saturation, tanh'(z) = 1 - tanh^2(z) drops well below 1, so the effective contraction can be < 1 even though rho(W_rec) > 1 (the chapter's x_{t+1}=tanh(2x_t+u_t) example has rho=2 yet the ESP holds). Option B inverts the fact: tanh' never exceeds 1, it only shrinks. The leak rate cancels out of the ESP condition, and rho<1 IS sufficient (necessary/sufficient only in the linear case), so A and C are wrong.
